svg.title: For a finite collection of edges these links depend analytically on the finite jet J near zero. One can see this without differentiating an infinite configuration map. The integral equation in matrix path space is u = 1 + VJu, where VJ is integration followed by multiplication by the connection. Near J = 0 its norm is less than one, so (1 −VJ)−1 = P n≥0 Vn J is analytic. Uniqueness identifies it R 1 0 AJ with (PF5). Differentiating at zero gives the edge tangent i (x + tei) dt. Products and inverse links therefore have tangents equal to their signed edge sums.
